newsitem.title: GERMANY: Modest cocoa buying interest seen in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Modest cocoa buying interest seen in Germany.

text.p: German cocoa consumers were placing orders for third/fourth quarter 1997 and first quarter 1998 beans against sharply lower futures, physical traders said on Wednesday.
"After weeks and months of inactivity, this is quite encouraging and historically, 1,000 stg on the second position is attractive," one said.
"But the strong British currency continues to deter buyers."
London futures hit two week lows on Tuesday and New York plunged to its lowest levels in eight weeks on speculative and technical factors as well as comfortable nearby supplies.
London July was last at 990 stg, down 11 from the close.
Traders did not believe in a free fall after forecasts of ample Ivorian main and mid-crops and a report from broker GNI Ltd anticipating a lower 1996/97 world deficit, if not a slight surplus.
"West African mid-crop progress appears hesitant and shipments are still delayed," one said.
"Asian crops are increasingly absorbed by domestic demand -- I don't believe in a change in fundamentals."
Cocoa butter demand was flat although the butter ratio over futures has fallen by 15 points over the last month.

The ratio was at 2.40 for spot, with some recent trades reported below that level. The ratio for other 1997 dates was 2.44, with implied mark prices 6.80 marks/kg liquid ex-works for second and third quarter and 6.90 for the fourth.
West African beans were quoted at 2.70-2.75 marks/kg cif, down from 2.81-2.86 a week ago.
Sterling was 2.8075 marks at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
